'''Alvin Virgil Tollestrup''' (March 22, 1924 – February 9, 2020) was an American high-energy particle physicist best known for his key roles in the development of the superconducting magnets for [[Fermilab]]'s [[Tevatron]] and the formation of [[Collider Detector at Fermilab|CDF]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Zweig|first=George|year=2020|title=Alvin Tollestrup 1924–2020: remembering a visionary physicist|url=https://cerncourier.com/a/remembering-alvin-tollestrup-1924-2020/|journal=CERN Courier|volume=60|issue=3|pages=63}}</ref>

==Biography==

Alvin Tollestrup was born in Los Angeles, California, on March 22, 1924.<ref name="ACAP">{{cite web |url = https://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?tollestrupa |title = Array of Contemporary American Physicists: Alvin Tollestrup |publisher = [[American Institute of Physics]] |date = 2016 |access-date = 31 May 2016 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160625032603/https://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?tollestrupa |archive-date = 25 June 2016 |url-status = dead }}</ref> He received a BS in engineering from the [[University of Utah]] in 1944. After graduating, he served in the U.S. Navy, where he studied and installed radar systems. After he was discharged, he entered the [[California Institute of Technology]]<ref name="Oral history">{{cite web |url = http://oralhistories.library.caltech.edu/229/1/Tollestrup%20OHO.pdf |title = Alvin V. Tollestrup (b. 1924), Interviewed by David A. Valone |publisher = [[California Institute of Technology]] Archives |date = 2014 |access-date= 31 May 2016 }}</ref> in 1946,<ref name="URA Fellow profile">{{cite web |url = http://www.fnal.gov/pub/forphysicists/fellowships/alvin_tollestrup/about.html |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150916080305/https://www.fnal.gov/pub/forphysicists/fellowships/alvin_tollestrup/about.html |url-status = dead |archive-date = September 16, 2015 |title = About Alvin Tollestrup |publisher = [[Fermilab]] |date = 25 February 2015 |access-date = 31 May 2016 }}</ref> where he worked with [[William Alfred Fowler]] and [[Charles Christian Lauritsen]]. He received his PhD in 1950. He remained at Caltech as a research fellow, eventually becoming an assistant professor of physics in 1953 and later a full professor.<ref name="Oral history" />

Tollestrup visited the [[CERN|European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN)]] in 1957/58 with a fellowship from the [[National Science Foundation]].<ref name="aipbio">{{cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11610015.html|title=Alvin Tollestrup|publisher=[[American Institute of Physics]]|website=AIP Physics History Network|access-date=2019-07-15}}</ref>

Tollestrup went to [[Fermilab]] on sabbatical in April 1975, intending to spend nine months at the lab. At the lab, he learned of Fermilab director [[Robert R. Wilson]]'s plans to build a superconducting accelerator, which would come to be called the [[Tevatron]]. Tollestrup began working with the group developing the superconducting magnets for the accelerator. As plans for the Tevatron progressed, Tollestrup was also involved in forming a group to study the experimental possibilities opened by the collider, a group which eventually became [[Collider Detector at Fermilab|CDF]]. Caltech extended his sabbatical to two years as he worked on these projects, but in 1977 Tollestrup had to choose whether to return to Caltech or remain at Fermilab. He decided to stay at Fermilab, where he continued to work on the development of the Tevatron, CDF,<ref name="Oral history" /> and Fermilab's colliding beams program. He won the [[National Medal of Technology and Innovation|National Medal of Technology]] in 1989 for his work on the design, testing, and commissioning of the Tevatron's superconducting magnets, which was the first large-scale application of superconductivity.<ref name="URA Fellow profile" /> He died on February 9, 2020, at the age of 95.<ref name="Remembering Alvin Tollestrup">{{cite web|url=https://news.fnal.gov/2020/02/remembering-alvin-tollestrup/|title=Remembering Alvin Tollestrup|publisher=[[Fermilab]]|website=fnal.gov|access-date=2020-02-10|archive-date=2020-03-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200302185700/https://news.fnal.gov/2020/02/remembering-alvin-tollestrup/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
